**Signal Processing Engineer**
Sinikaari Optics, Oulu | 2005 - present

- Designed and executed RF measurement campaigns for photonic sensor front ends, including S-parameter characterisation of prototype modules using Rohde & Schwarz vector network analysers and automated swept-frequency test sequences

Led a three-person engineering sub-team through the firmware validation and CE-marking documentation phase, coordinating between Sinikaari's sensor group and the medical-device client (a German university hospital).

Finnish citizen; the project was delivered under an EU-funded cross-border health technology programme.

Applied spectral analysis and filter design methods grounded in my electrical engineering background throughout the project, particularly in the band-selection and rejection filter stages.

application.cover_letter_markdown:
I noticed the Senior Signal Processing Engineer opening at Kaikuvaara and wanted to write. Twenty years at Sinikaari Optics, all of them in Oulu, is the short version of my CV, but the longer version is probably more useful to you.

Most of my work at Sinikaari has been in sensor systems -- photonic front ends, acoustic arrays, and one detour into medical wearables that turned out to be the most technically interesting project I have done. The common thread is taking noisy analogue signals, getting them into a digital domain cleanly, and building the processing chain that makes them useful to whoever sits downstream. At Sinikaari that has ranged from RF bench characterisation of individual sensor modules, where I have spent more time with network analysers than I could reasonably explain at a dinner party, through to maintaining the Python calibration pipeline that runs nightly on our production floor. The pipeline handles batch testing, archiving, and automated pass/fail decisions, and it has been in continuous use since 2018.

The medical ECG/EEG front-end project (2017-2019) was where things came together most completely. We had hard latency constraints, strict noise floors defined by the clinical application, and a three-person firmware team I was responsible for coordinating through validation testing and CE-marking documentation. I saw every phase of that project, from initial feasibility through hardware bring-up, algorithm development, integration testing, and the paperwork that goes with medical-device certification. The end product shipped and is still in clinical use at two sites in Germany. That kind of full-cycle delivery is what I am most interested in continuing.

On the sensor side, I have built beamformers for acoustic arrays and spent enough time doing RF measurements to know the difference between a real problem and a cable issue. Sinikaari has given me a solid grounding in what production-grade sensor characterisation actually involves, and the calibration pipeline I mentioned is the system currently running on the factory floor -- reliable, documented, and maintained rather than clever. That probably says more about how I work than any technology list would.

I am interested in Kaikuvaara because Oulu's sensor engineering community is small enough that you hear about what people are building nearby, and the technical scope you describe seems well-matched to my background. I have been here twenty years and plan to stay. If you are looking for someone who can contribute from day one without a relocation delay or a ramp-up in the domain, I would welcome the conversation.

Jari Hamalainen

application.cover_letter_markdown:
The Senior Signal Processing Engineer role at Kaikuvaara caught my eye partly because of the Oulu connection. I have been living and working here since 2011, when I joined Sumuvire Wireless after finishing at Rheinmark TU Aachen, and the city has become home in a way I did not expect when I first moved back to Finland. The RF and photonics engineering community here is small enough that you end up knowing a fair number of people across companies, and I have always liked that about working in this region.

At Sumuvire my main responsibility has been RF characterisation of wireless transceiver modules. This is hands-on measurement work -- spectrum analysers, vector network analysers, the anechoic test setup we built up from fairly basic equipment over the years. I have run hundreds of radiated emission tests per CTSI standards and done the documentation and reporting that goes along with compliance work for international customers. It is detail-oriented and sometimes repetitive, but it has taught me a lot about what actually matters when a wireless module goes to production.

One project I am particularly glad I got to work on was embedded DSP firmware for Sumuvire's next-generation transceiver. I wrote the real-time channel estimation and interference mitigation routines in C running on a TI C6748 DSP, working closely with the RF hardware team to make sure the filter coefficients actually matched what we were seeing on the bench. That was probably the most technically demanding thing I have done at Sumuvire, and it confirmed for me that I enjoy the embedded side of signal processing as much as the measurement side. I would like to do more of it.

I will be straightforward about the fact that my background is in mechanical engineering rather than EE. At RMTU I focused on dynamics and vibration measurement, which is further from your work than I would like. The transition to RF and wireless at Sumuvire was steep at the start but by now I have spent fifteen years in the domain. Whether that counts as equivalent experience in your assessment is obviously your call.

What draws me to Kaikuvaara specifically is the chance to work on more complex signal processing systems than what Sumuvire's product line requires. I do not know the details of your current projects, but the job description suggests the kind of work I have been wanting to move toward. Oulu is where I plan to stay regardless, so geography is easy.

I would welcome the chance to speak with you about whether my profile is a reasonable fit.

Mikko Lehtonen

What I would argue is that those four years have been intense and hands-on in exactly the domains your role requires. I have been the primary signal processing engineer on our receiver chain since joining, which means I have had the kind of end-to-end responsibility that people at larger companies sometimes do not get until much later. Whether that compensates for the shorter timeline is obviously your call, but I wanted to address it directly rather than hope it goes unnoticed.

I look forward to discussing the role.

Antti Kinnunen

## Work Experience

**Signal Processing Engineer**
Hallaharju Space Systems, Oulu | 2018 - present

- Designed and implemented phased-array beamforming algorithms for a 64-element UHF receive array, including broadband time-delay beamforming and sidelobe control for the company's ground-based monitoring product line
- Developed embedded DSP firmware in C/C++ for the array processing unit, running on an ADSP-21489 SHARC processor; responsible for the full pipeline from ADC capture through frequency-domain beamforming output

- Working language at Hallaharju Space Systems is English; I conduct all technical discussions, design reviews, and client presentations in English
- Relocated from Germany to Oulu in 2018 to take this position; have been based here continuously since

## Selected Projects

**Array Calibration Toolchain** (2021-2022)

Developed a field-calibration procedure and supporting analysis tools for the 64-element UHF array. The work drew heavily on my RMTU coursework in electromagnetic field theory and antenna design, and the calibration methodology was based on the coupling-matrix approach I studied during my master's thesis.

## Skills

- Python: developed and maintain a pytest-based integration test suite for the beamformer firmware (~5k lines), plus calibration analysis scripts; deployed on the team's GitLab CI pipeline
- MATLAB, Simulink

application.cover_letter_markdown:
When I moved from Germany to Oulu in 2018 to join Hallaharju Space Systems, the draw was purely technical: I wanted to work on phased arrays, and Hallaharju's ground-based monitoring systems used exactly the kind of dense receive arrays I had written my master's thesis on at RMTU. Eight years later, the job has delivered on that promise and then some.

My path into signal processing was through electromagnetics. At RMTU I studied antenna theory and EM field simulation, and my thesis dealt with mutual coupling compensation in dense arrays -- the gap between the ideal pattern and what you actually measure when 64 elements are packed into a tight aperture. At Hallaharju I have been able to apply that work directly, first in building the calibration methodology for our UHF receive array and then in the broader signal processing chain: beamforming, interference rejection, and the embedded firmware that runs it all.

The role at Hallaharju has been unusually broad for a single position. I write the DSP firmware, run the RF measurement campaigns when we bring up new hardware, maintain the test infrastructure, and handle the calibration data pipeline. That breadth is partly a consequence of being in a small team, but I have come to see it as a real strength in my profile. I have spent as much time at the bench with a VNA and probe fixtures as I have at a desk writing code, and I think that combination is what makes me effective at the system level rather than just in one slice of it.

The reason I am looking at Kaikuvaara is that I would like to do similar work with more resources behind it. Hallaharju is a good company but the team is small and the product line is narrow. After eight years I have worked on essentially one array architecture in depth. Kaikuvaara's scope suggests a wider variety of systems and, I would hope, more engineers to learn from and collaborate with. Oulu is where I live and want to continue living, so geography is not a factor in this decision.

I do not have a tidy narrative about climbing a career ladder, because that is not what the last eight years have looked like. What I do have is deep, hands-on experience in exactly the technical areas your role describes: phased-array processing, embedded firmware for real-time DSP, RF measurement and calibration, and the tooling that holds a development workflow together. Most of that experience has been acquired by being the person who has to figure something out because no one else on the team had done it before, which is perhaps not the worst way to learn.

I would be happy to discuss specific projects or go through technical details at your convenience.

Ingrid Andersson

application.cover_letter_markdown:
Fourteen years in signal processing, most of it at Hohtola Photonics in Oulu, is what I would bring to this role. The embedded and RF measurement work I have done at Hohtola before and after that period fills in the rest of the picture.

My CRIT master's in electrical engineering and computer science gave me the analytical grounding -- the signal processing theory and linear algebra that every beamformer and matched filter ultimately rests on. The fourteen years since have been about applying that foundation in real hardware systems with real noise floors and real timing constraints.

I have maintained an interest in publishing and in contributing to open-source signal processing projects, and I believe the combination of academic grounding and production experience is what distinguishes a senior engineer from someone who is merely experienced.

Oulu is home. I have lived here since 2012 apart from eight months in Tampere at Nordtek, and I am not looking to move. Kaikuvaara's location here is a straightforward advantage from my perspective.

Happy to discuss specifics in person.

Marko Turunen
